title: Containment Checklists and Post-Incident Learning Path
author: Marco Chen
summary: Actionable containment checklists for common Redwood incident classes plus a structured post-incident learning path and governance checklist. This page is the single-source reference for first-responder actions, communications cadence, and how to convert incidents into prioritized engineering work and measurable improvements.
audience: On-call engineers, SREs, incident commanders, product and CS leads responsible for customer communications, and owners of production services.
overview: This document provides concise, role-oriented containment checklists (what to do in the first 30/60/120 minutes), a severity classification table tied to SLO impact, a template cadence for internal and external communications, and the Post-Incident Learning Path that turns incidents into tracked improvements. Use these checklists immediately when an incident is suspected; escalate to the Incident Commander (IC) when a checklist does not restore service within the first containment window.
incident-classification-and-slos:
Severity | Customer Impact | Typical SLO Signal | Target Response Window
--------|----------------|-------------------|------------------------
P0 (Sev-0) | Complete service outage for a region or global failure (API returns 5xx or timeouts) | >=20% error rate or >3x latency SLO breach | Page IC and begin containment within 5 minutes
P1 (Sev-1) | Major feature degraded for many customers (model generation timeouts, heavy token backlogs) | 5-20% error or 2-3x latency SLO breach | Acknowledge and begin containment within 15 minutes
P2 (Sev-2) | Partial degradation or single-region/tenant impact; mitigations available | Degraded tail latency or increased token cost by >25% | Begin investigation within 1 hour
P3 (Sev-3) | Minor, non-customer-impacting anomalies or alerts with no clear customer effect | Metric deviation without SLA breach | Triage in next on-call shift

SLO references: API latency p50/p95 targets are defined per service in /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets; use those thresholds when classifying severity.
containment-checklists:
CONTAINMENT CHECKLIST - FIRST 30 MINUTES (P0/P1)
1) Triage and establish the channel
   - Confirm error signature (5xx, auth failure, model OOM, network error). Use metrics: api_gateway.errors_total, runtime.oom_events, queue.depth.
   - Create incident channel: #incident-<service>-<region>-<sequential-id>. Add IC, on-call, product owner, CS lead.
2) Stabilize customer impact
   - Apply immediate traffic policy: route traffic to fallback model variant or healthy region (smart routing runbook).
   - If load-induced: enable request shedding for non-critical endpoints (X-Delay header or token-budget enforcement).
   - If model OOMs: scale up worker JVM/GPU memory profile OR switch to lower-memory quantized variant.
3) Short-term mitigation commands (examples)
   - kubectl rollout pause deployment/<service> -n production
   - curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/route-redirection -d '{"from":"us-east-1","to":"us-west-2","policy":"read-only"}'
   - redis-cli FT.SEARCH incident_cache "*" --truncate 0  (check backlog)
4) Validate customer-facing recovery
   - Confirm 200 responses for health-check endpoint /_health and a drop in 5xxs for 5 consecutive minutes.

CONTAINMENT CHECKLIST - FIRST 2 HOURS (P0/P1)
1) Deep triage and metrics correlation
   - Correlate traces (jaeger) with error spikes; search for recent deploys or config changes.
   - Check autoscaling and GPU utilization dashboards (Grafana panels: inference/gpu_util_pct, inference/queue_depth).
2) Revert or patch
   - If recent deploy suspected: revert to prior stable tag and monitor.
   - If configuration error: apply hotfix via config-management and restart routing proxies.
3) Communicate
   - IC posts an initial incident summary within 30 minutes. Use the INTERNAL UPDATE template below.
4) Escalation criteria
   - If service still degraded after 2 hours, prepare cross-team war room and notify exec on-call.

CONTAINMENT CHECKLIST - MODEL QUALITY REGRESSION (P1/P2)
1) Quick isolation
   - Pull recent model variant rollout logs and compare eval metrics for the latest prompts.
   - Temporarily pin traffic to previous model version in the catalog.
2) For generation hallucination spikes
   - Adjust decoding parameters (temperature=0.2, top_k=40) via the dynamic policy service.
   - Apply prompt-anchoring guardrails (prefix template) if available.
3) Monitor and rollback
   - Watch quality evaluation dashboard (prompt-evals/regressions) and customer tickets for improvement.

SECURITY-TYPE INCIDENT (DATA/ACCESS) - FIRST STEPS
1) Preserve evidence
   - Do NOT restart affected hosts. Snapshot volumes and capture process lists.
2) Notify Security@Redwood and follow the Security Incident Response runbook.
3) If data exfiltration suspected: rotate affected keys and revoke sessions.
runbook-invocation-and-tools:
RUNBOOK INVOCATION
1) Who may run: on-call engineer, IC, SRE lead.
2) Invocation steps: create incident channel + set incident channel topic to severity, short summary, and link to this runbook.
3) Tagging convention: add label 'active-incident' and include 'ic:<name>' in the channel topic.

COMMON COMMANDS & SNIPPETS- Check API error rate:
  curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/api/query?expr=rate(api_gateway_errors_total[5m])' | jq
- Re-route traffic (control plane):
  rwctl route set --service inference --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --policy emergency-fallback
- Pin model version via catalog API:
  curl -X PATCH https://catalog.internal/models/my-model/traffic -d '{"pin_version":"v20260110-rc"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

NOTES ON TOOLING
- Use the Incident Manager UI only for ticketing and follow-up action items; real-time coordination should occur in the chat channel for speed.
- All critical commands must be run by at least two team members when the incident is classified P0/P1 (safety check).
post-incident-learning-path:
POST-INCIDENT LEARNING PATH (objectives -> outputs -> timelines)
1) Immediate (within 24 hours)
   - Incident log: IC compiles a timeline with timestamps and key actions.
   - Action item creation: convert immediate fixes into tracked JIRA tasks and tag with 'incident:<id>'.
2) Postmortem (within 3 business days)
   - Draft a blameless postmortem covering: summary, timeline, impact, root cause analysis, action items, and risk assessment.
   - Required reviewers: IC, service owner, SRE lead, product manager, and customer success rep.
3) Learning artifacts (within 10 business days)
   - Runbook updates: add missing steps or clarify ambiguous commands.
   - Create a short internal HowItWasFixed note for knowledge-sharing (1-2 page).
   - Schedule a 60-minute 'learning sync' in the owning team to review changes and proposed experiments.
4) Closure and measurement (30 days)
   - Verify action items: owners must post progress updates and link evidence (tests, dashboards).
   - Measure regression risk: run synthetic tests and compare to pre-incident baselines; mark postmortem as closed only when regression risk is mitigated or accepted.

POSTMORTEM TEMPLATE (short)- Title, Incident ID, Date, Severity, Summary (1-2 sentences)- Impact (customers affected, minutes of downtime)- Timeline (concise chronology)- Root cause hypothesis and evidence- Actions (owner, due date, verification steps)- Signal improvements (what metrics will show success)- Link to runbook changes and testing artifacts
synthetic-testing-and-game-days:
SYNTHETIC TESTING STRATEGY
- Objective: detect regressions to latency, throughput, and quality before customers are affected.
- Tests to run: per-region health probes, end-to-end generation sampling (10 prompts x 1000 calls/day), cold-start latency sweep, KV-cache hit-rate tests.
- Frequency: lightweight probes every 1 minute; heavier E2E suite every 6 hours; full-day smoke every Sunday.

GAME DAY SCHEDULING & BLUEPRINT
- Quarterly tabletop exercise: 2-hour session, 1 IC per simulated incident, cross-team observers.
- Annual full-scale simulation: 4-hour live exercise with customer comms mock, status page fake incidents, and exec on-call observer.
- Post-game-day outputs: After-action report, runbook updates, and mandatory learning session for participants.
communication-templates:
INTERNAL UPDATE (first 30 minutes)
- Subject: [INCIDENT] <service> - <short impact> - <region>
- Body: 1) Current status (what we see), 2) Actions taken, 3) Next steps, 4) Owner / IC, 5) Estimated time to next update.

CUSTOMER STATUS PAGE TEMPLATE (initial)
- Title: Service disruption affecting <service> in <region>
- Summary: We are investigating increased errors and latency affecting API requests in <region>. No data loss is suspected at this time.
- Current status: Investigating
- Impact: Customers may experience failed requests or elevated latency.
- Next update: <ETA or timeframe>
- Contact: support@redwood.ai (for affected customers request priority support)

CUSTOMER UPDATE (30-90 minutes)
- Clear summary of what changed and what customers should expect. If workaround exists, provide concrete steps (e.g., set region header to us-west-2). Avoid technical internal-only jargon.

EXECUTIVE ESCALATION NOTE
- 1-line impact, estimated revenue/customer SLA risk, critical path to recovery, ask (resources/approvals).
runbook-governance-and-maintenance:
GOVERNANCE CHECKS
- Owners: Each runbook must have a named owner and a backup. Owners are responsible for quarterly verification.
- Review cadence: Quarterly review for critical runbooks (P0/P1), annual for lower severity. Document results in the runbook header.
- Test coverage: Every runbook must include at least one synthetic test or game-day scenario that verifies the primary containment steps.
- Decommissioning: Mark runbooks 'deprecated' and archive them with a linked rationale when services are retired.

ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES (quick)
- Incident Commander (IC): control channel, decide severity, own external comms.
- On-call engineer: execute containment steps, run commands, feed timeline.
- SRE lead: cross-team coordination and postmortem signoff.
- Product/CS rep: customer-facing updates and ticket prioritization.
appendix-and-checklists:
APPENDIX A: QUICK CHECKLIST CARD (copy into chat when incident starts)
- Create channel and set topic
- Confirm error signature & severity
- Apply emergency routing/fallback
- Validate recovery (health endpoint & 5xx reduction)
- Post initial internal update

APPENDIX B: QUICK STATUS PAGE JSON (example){
  "incident_id": "INC-20260218-001",
  "service": "inference-api",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "status": "investigating",
  "next_update": "2026-02-18T15:30:00Z"
}

APPENDIX C: SAMPLE JIRA LABELS
- incident-2026, severity-p0, area-runtime, owner-sre, hotfix-required
conclusion: Containment is the priority for the first 2 hours; learning and prevention are the long-term goals. Use this page as the canonical checklist for first responders and follow the Post-Incident Learning Path to ensure incidents produce durable improvements. If you identify gaps in these procedures, open an action item and tag it 'runbook:review' so it will be triaged in the next runbook governance cycle.
how_to_edit: To propose changes: 1) Fork the runbook draft in the Runbook Editor, 2) Add your rationale as a comment, 3) Request review from the owners and one SRE reviewer. Changes to P0/P1 steps require at least two reviewers before publishing.
